title: Regional Read Replicas vs. Edge Caching for Analytics
question: Should we deploy cross-region PostgreSQL read replicas or add a Redis edge cache layer to cut p95 dashboard latency below 180ms?
executiveSummary: Current telemetry indicates that 78% of p95 latency (640ms) originates from repeated analytical aggregation queries rather than network round-trips across regions. Deploying a structured cache-aside layer with short TTLs and materialized rollups addresses the root bottleneck at roughly one-third the monthly infrastructure cost of cross-region read replicas.
recommendation: Implement incremental materialized rollups paired with regional Redis edge caching for the top 12 dashboard queries in Phase 1, and defer cross-region PostgreSQL read replicas until write throughput or strict zero-staleness compliance requires them.

findings.title: Aggregation Scans Dominate Query Time
findings.summary: Slow query logs show 90-day tenant rollups scanning 14M+ rows repeatedly during morning login spikes, accounting for 490ms of the 640ms p95 budget.
findings.evidence: Production pg_stat_statements snapshot across 48 hours of peak traffic.

findings.title: Cross-Region Replication Adds Write & Cost Overhead
findings.summary: Running two additional db.r6g.xlarge read replicas across EU and APAC adds ~$1,840/month before cross-region WAL transfer fees.
findings.evidence: Q3 cloud billing estimates and WAL generation baseline (42 GB/day).

findings.title: Dashboard SLA Permits 30-Second Freshness Window
findings.summary: Product stakeholders confirmed executive KPI cards only need near-real-time updates, whereas billing exports require primary DB consistency.
findings.evidence: Engineering & Product sync notes from Nov 10 architecture review.

findings.title: Stale Cache Invalidation Needs Tenant Scoping
findings.summary: Shared cache keys without explicit workspace IDs and permission hashes risk cross-tenant data leakage during role updates.
findings.evidence: Security checklist item SEC-19 from internal platform audit.

risks.risk: Thundering herd on cache expiration during 09:00 UTC spikes
risks.mitigation: Use stale-while-revalidate (SWR) locking with jittered TTLs (+/- 15%) on rollup keys.

risks.risk: Drift between cached dashboard totals and CSV export totals
risks.mitigation: Route all CSV/audit exports directly to the primary replica and display last-refreshed timestamps on dashboard cards.

risks.risk: Redis memory eviction under sudden tenant onboarding surge
risks.mitigation: Configure allkeys-lru eviction policy and cap per-tenant cached payload size at 256 KB.

actions.task: Create incremental hourly rollup tables for top 12 analytics widgets
Implement tenant-scoped Redis cache wrapper with SWR jitter
Add explicit Last Updated timestamp to executive dashboard header
Run k6 load test simulating 5x morning login spike in staging

rawNotes:
Architecture sync notes:
- Current p95 dashboard load: 640ms (target <180ms).
- pg_stat_statements: 78% of time is spent in 90-day tenant rollup aggregations scanning ~14M rows.
- WAL volume is 42 GB/day. Two cross-region replicas (EU + APAC) estimated at ~$1,840/mo + egress.
- Product confirmed 30s staleness is fine for charts, NOT fine for billing/audit CSV exports.
- Security requires strict tenant_id + role_version in any cache key.

thread.content: What happens if a workspace admin revokes a user permission while a cached response is still warm?

Because authorization checks happen at the API gateway before reading from the cache, a revoked user is rejected before any cached payload is returned. Including `role_version` in the cache key (as noted in Finding 4) provides defense-in-depth so even permission-scoped sub-queries cannot serve prior-role aggregations.

title: Q1 Enterprise AI Assistant Governance & Audit Readiness
question: What technical controls and vendor policies must be finalized before rolling out customer-facing document summarization to regulated EU enterprise accounts?
executiveSummary: Regulated EU enterprise procurement teams increasingly require verifiable zero-data-retention guarantees, explicit human-in-the-loop review boundaries for high-stakes outputs, and exportable prompt/response audit trails before signing annual contracts. Closing these three compliance gaps unblocks four late-stage enterprise pilots without delaying the core Q1 product launch.
recommendation: Ship workspace-level Zero Data Retention (ZDR) routing, immutable audit logs for generated summaries, and clear source-citation links on every extracted claim prior to the Q1 enterprise pilot cohort.

findings.title: Zero Data Retention Is a Procurement Blocker
findings.summary: Three of four EU financial services prospects listed zero model-training retention and EU regional processing endpoints as mandatory InfoSec sign-off criteria.
findings.evidence: Enterprise security questionnaires from Q4 pipeline reviews.

findings.title: Citation Grounding Cuts Manual Review Time by Half
findings.summary: Beta testers spent significantly less time verifying AI summaries when each bullet linked directly to the underlying paragraph or uploaded document page.
findings.evidence: Internal pilot feedback across 18 compliance analysts.

findings.title: Automated Decisions Require Explicit Disclaimers
findings.summary: Advisory summaries must clearly separate extracted facts from model-inferred recommendations so analysts retain documented decision accountability.
findings.evidence: Legal counsel memo on enterprise AI transparency labeling.

risks.risk: PII inadvertently logged in standard application error traces
risks.mitigation: Scrub prompt/document payloads from structured exception loggers and route audit metadata through encrypted EU storage.

risks.risk: Sales team commits to custom on-prem deployment timelines
risks.mitigation: Publish a standardized VPC/EU-resident cloud architecture brief for account executives.
